title_o: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice

replications.journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
replications.quote: In the aggregate replication sample (N = 7,228), participants were more likely to say that they would go to the other branch when the cheap item was on sale (49%) than when the costly item was on sale (32%; p = 1.01e−50, d = 0.40, 95% CI = [0.35, 0.45]; OR = 2.06, 95% CI = [1.87, 2.27]). These results are consistent with the hypothesis that the base cost of a discounted item influences willingness to travel, though the effect was less than half the size of the original (OR = 2.06, 95% CI = [1.87, 2.27], vs. original OR = 4.96).
